result.title: The Format is the Filter: Scoring Format Fixes What an LLM Judge Can Express
result.summary: When an LLM judge filters instruction-tuning data, its scoring format (binary verdict, 1--5 rating, 0--100 score, or comparison) is rarely justified or ablated. Holding the candidate pool, judge prompt, decoding and selection budget fixed, we score 15,406 UltraFeedback candidates under five formats with three judges, curate, fine-tune 66 models, and evaluate them with four judges. A 0--100 scale is worth only 7--12 equally used levels, two to three times a 1--5 scale rather than twenty, and a binary verdict leaves the top score tied in 77--78\% of prompts, so most selections are made at random. These properties are set by the format almost independently of the judge. Kendall's $τ_b$ hides them: it ranks binary best while $τ_a$ and top-1 agreement rank it last, because it discounts the ties a selector must break at random. Both comparative formats inherit a slot bias whose sign differs across judges. Downstream, curated data beat random selection under every evaluation judge, robust to length and markdown adjustment, but no ordering among formats is detectable. We propose four quantities that judge-based curation pipelines should report.

AI.brief_summary: 论文固定候选池、判官提示与解码预算，用三种 LLM judge、五种打分格式（二值、1–5、0–100、比较）为 15,406 条 UltraFeedback 数据打分，微调 66 个模型并评测，发现格式几乎独立地决定可用判别层级与并列比例，并提出四项应报告的量。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文讨论打分「格式」本身限定了判官可表达的信息、导致大量并列只能随机取舍，并揭示排序指标会掩盖这一点；这可能为 LVR 中奖励／验证信号的设计与评估（格式约束下的判别力与随机选择）提供可核查的类比线索，但本身不涉及 latent 推理状态。
